items.plain: Light is sweet and seeing the sun is good. However many years a person lives, they should enjoy them all, yet remember that dark days will be many, and everything that comes passes away.
items.core_idea: Enjoy every year, but remember dark days will come

items.plain: You may be angry, but do not let it lead you into sin. Settle your anger before the day ends, and give the devil no foothold.
items.core_idea: Do not let anger last past sundown

items.plain: Say nothing harmful. Speak only words that build others up when they need it, so that your words are a gift to those who hear them.
items.core_idea: Speak only words that build others up

items.plain: Get rid of all bitterness, rage, anger, shouting, slander and malice. Be kind and tender-hearted to one another, and forgive each other just as God forgave you in Christ.
items.core_idea: Drop bitterness; forgive as God forgave you

items.plain: Fathers, do not push your children into anger; raise them with the discipline and teaching of the Lord.
items.core_idea: Do not provoke children; raise them in the Lord

items.plain: Lord, you alone are our king. Help me: I am alone, with no one to help me but you, and danger is close.
items.core_idea: A plea to God when alone and in danger

items.plain: God who rules over all, hear those who have lost hope. Save us from those plotting harm, and free me from my fear.
items.core_idea: A prayer to God for rescue from fear

items.plain: Who knows whether you came to your position for exactly this moment?
items.core_idea: You may be where you are for this moment

items.plain: The king of Egypt ordered the Hebrew midwives to kill every baby boy at birth. But the midwives feared God more than the king, refused the order, and let the boys live.
items.core_idea: Fear of God gave the midwives courage to disobey

items.plain: Moses told God he was a poor speaker. God replied that he made every human mouth, and told Moses to go, promising to be with his mouth and teach him what to say.
items.core_idea: God helps the one who feels unable to speak

items.plain: Moses went back to God and complained: why have you brought trouble on this people and sent me? Since I spoke to Pharaoh for you, things have got worse, and you have not rescued them.
items.core_idea: Moses honestly complains to God when things worsen

items.plain: God will fight for you; you only need to be still.
items.core_idea: God will fight for you; be still

items.plain: God is my strength and my song, and has saved me. He is my God and my father's God, and I will praise him.
items.core_idea: God is my strength, song and salvation

items.plain: Moses' father-in-law told him that what he was doing was not good: he would wear out himself and the people, because the load was too heavy to carry alone.
items.core_idea: The load is too heavy to carry alone

items.plain: Do not crave what belongs to your neighbour: not their house, their spouse, their workers, their animals, or anything else that is theirs.
items.core_idea: Do not crave what belongs to others

items.plain: Do not join a crowd in doing wrong. In court, do not go along with the majority to twist justice.
items.core_idea: Do not follow the crowd into wrongdoing

items.plain: If you find your enemy's animal wandering, take it back to him. If you see the donkey of someone who hates you collapsed under its load, do not walk away; help him with it.
items.core_idea: Help even your enemy when he is in trouble

items.plain: Do not take bribes: a bribe blinds people who can see and twists the words of honest people.
items.core_idea: Bribes blind and corrupt even the honest

items.plain: Do not mistreat a foreigner. You know how a foreigner feels, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
items.core_idea: Do not mistreat foreigners; you were one

items.plain: God proclaims his own name: merciful, gracious, slow to anger, full of steadfast love and truth, forgiving wrongdoing, yet not letting the guilty go unpunished, with consequences reaching to later generations.
items.core_idea: God is merciful and forgiving, yet holds guilt accountable

items.plain: God promises to give his people one heart and a new spirit, replacing their hearts of stone with hearts of flesh, so they will follow his ways; they will be his people and he their God.
items.core_idea: God will replace hearts of stone with living hearts

items.plain: God says to Israel, pictured as an abandoned newborn: when I passed by and saw you lying in your blood, I told you to live, even there in your blood.
items.core_idea: God told the helpless one: live

items.plain: Sodom's wrongdoing was this: pride, too much food, and comfortable ease, while she did nothing to help the poor and needy.
items.core_idea: Comfort without helping the poor is wrongdoing

items.plain: The person who sins is the one who dies. A child will not carry a parent's guilt, nor a parent a child's; each person's goodness or wickedness is their own.
items.core_idea: Each person answers for their own deeds

items.plain: If a wicked person turns from their sins and does right, they will live; their past wrongs will not be held against them. God takes no pleasure in the wicked dying; he wants them to turn back and live.
items.core_idea: God wants the wrongdoer to turn back and live

items.plain: Throw off all your wrongdoing and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why die? God says he takes no pleasure in anyone's death, so turn back and live.
items.core_idea: Turn from wrongdoing, make a new heart, and live

items.plain: Your beauty made you proud, and your splendour corrupted your wisdom.
items.core_idea: Pride in beauty corrupts wisdom

items.plain: The people say their sins weigh on them and they are wasting away, so how can they live? God answers that he wants not the death of the wicked but their turning: turn back, why die?
items.core_idea: Weighed down by sin? God says turn and live

items.plain: People come and listen to you as if devoted, praising you with their mouths while their hearts chase profit. To them you are just a pleasant song: they hear your words but do not act on them.
items.core_idea: People enjoy hearing truth but do not act on it

items.plain: Shame on the leaders who look after only themselves. They take the best for themselves but neglect the weak, the sick, the injured, the strayed and the lost, and rule them harshly instead.
items.core_idea: Leaders who serve themselves neglect the vulnerable

items.plain: God says he will look for the lost, bring back the strays, bandage the injured and strengthen the sick, but destroy the fat and strong, and care for his flock with justice.
items.core_idea: God seeks the lost and heals the broken

items.plain: God promises a new heart and a new spirit: he will take away your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
items.core_idea: God will give you a new heart

items.plain: When the new temple's foundation was laid, the old who remembered the first temple wept aloud while many others shouted for joy, and no one could tell the joyful shouts from the weeping.
items.core_idea: Joy and grief can sound the same

items.plain: My God, I am too ashamed to lift my face to you; our wrongs have piled up over our heads and our guilt reaches the sky.
items.core_idea: Ashamed before God of guilt piled high

items.plain: Get up, because this task is yours, and we are with you. Be brave and do it.
items.core_idea: The task is yours; be brave, we're with you

items.plain: Am I trying to win people's approval, or God's? If I were still trying to please people, I would not be a servant of Christ.
items.core_idea: Seeking to please people conflicts with serving Christ

items.plain: In Christ Jesus there is no Jew or Greek, slave or free, male or female: you are all one.
items.core_idea: All are one in Christ Jesus

items.plain: You were called to freedom, but do not use it to indulge yourselves; serve one another in love. The whole law comes down to loving your neighbour as yourself. If you attack each other, you will destroy each other.
items.core_idea: Use freedom to serve one another in love

items.plain: What the Spirit produces is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. No law stands against these.
items.core_idea: The Spirit produces love, joy, peace and more

items.plain: If the Spirit gives us life, let us also live by the Spirit. Let us not become conceited, provoke one another, or envy one another.
items.core_idea: Live by the Spirit; avoid conceit and envy

items.plain: If someone slips into wrongdoing, the spiritual should gently restore them, watching their own temptation. Carry each other's burdens. Do not think yourself important; test your own work instead of comparing, since each carries their own load.
items.core_idea: Gently restore others; carry burdens; judge only yourself

items.plain: God is not mocked: you reap what you sow. Living for your appetites yields decay; living by the Spirit yields eternal life. So do not tire of doing good, because the harvest will come if you do not give up.
items.core_idea: You reap what you sow; don't tire of doing good

items.plain: God said it is not good for the man to be alone, and that he would make him a fitting partner.
items.core_idea: It is not good to be alone

items.plain: You will work hard for your food all your life until you go back to the ground you were made from, because you are dust and will return to dust.
items.core_idea: You are dust and will return to dust

items.plain: God asked Cain why he was angry and downcast. If he did right, he would be lifted up; if not, sin was lying in wait at his door, wanting him, but he must master it.
items.core_idea: Sin waits at the door; you must master it

items.plain: As long as the earth lasts, planting and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will never stop.
items.core_idea: The seasons and days will keep coming

items.plain: God told Abram to leave his country, his relatives and his father's home, and go to a land God would show him.
items.core_idea: Leave the familiar for where God leads

items.plain: Abram asked Lot not to let any quarrel come between them or their workers, since they were family. The whole land was open: Lot could choose a direction, and Abram would take the other.
items.core_idea: Give way rather than quarrel with family

items.plain: God spoke to Abram in a vision: do not be afraid; I am your shield and your great reward.
items.core_idea: Do not be afraid; God is your shield

items.plain: Jacob woke and said that God was surely in this place and he had not known it. Filled with awe, he called it the house of God and the gate of heaven.
items.core_idea: God was here, and I did not know

items.plain: Jacob worked seven years to marry Rachel, and they felt like only a few days because he loved her so much.
items.core_idea: Love made seven years feel like days

items.plain: Jacob, alone, wrestled with a man until dawn. Unable to win, the man injured Jacob's hip and asked to be let go as day broke, but Jacob said he would not let go unless the man blessed him.
items.core_idea: Hold on until you are blessed

items.plain: Esau told his brother that he already had enough, and Jacob should keep what was his.
items.core_idea: I have enough; keep what is yours

items.plain: Jacob tore his clothes and mourned his son for many days. All his children tried to comfort him, but he refused, saying he would grieve until he joined his son in the grave.
items.core_idea: A father refuses comfort in his grief

items.plain: Joseph named his first son to say God had made him forget his hardship and his father's house, and his second to say God had made him fruitful in the land where he suffered.
items.core_idea: God made me fruitful in the land of my suffering

items.plain: The brothers admitted to one another that they were guilty: they had seen their brother's anguish when he begged them and would not listen, and now this trouble had come on them.
items.core_idea: Ignoring another's anguish brings guilt back on you

items.plain: Overcome with love for his brother, Joseph hurried away to find somewhere to cry. He wept in his room, washed his face, steadied himself, came back and ordered the meal served.
items.core_idea: Joseph wept privately, then composed himself

items.plain: Joseph told his brothers who he was, the brother they had sold into Egypt. He said not to be upset or angry with themselves, because God had sent him ahead to save lives.
items.core_idea: God used the wrong done to me to save lives

items.plain: Asked his age, Jacob told Pharaoh his life's journey had lasted 130 years, and that his days had been few and hard, shorter than the lives of his ancestors.
items.core_idea: My days have been few and hard

items.plain: Israel told Joseph he never expected to see his face again, and now God had let him see Joseph's children too.
items.core_idea: I never thought I'd see you; now your children too

items.plain: Joseph threw himself on his dead father's face, wept over him and kissed him.
items.core_idea: A son weeps over his dead father

items.plain: Joseph told his brothers not to fear, since he was not God. They meant to harm him, but God meant it for good, to save many lives. He promised to provide for them, and spoke kindly to them.
items.core_idea: You meant harm, but God meant it for good

items.plain: How long, God, must I cry out before you listen? I shout about violence and you do not save. Why make me watch wrongdoing, destruction and conflict all around?
items.core_idea: How long, God, must I cry unheard?

items.plain: God told the prophet to write the vision clearly so anyone could read it quickly. It is for a set time and will not fail; though it seems slow, wait for it, because it will surely come.
items.core_idea: Though it seems slow, wait; it will come

items.plain: Even if the fig trees, vines, olives and fields all fail, and the flocks and herds are gone, I will still rejoice in God my saviour. The Lord is my strength and makes me sure-footed on the heights.
items.core_idea: Even when everything fails, I will rejoice in God

items.plain: Think about how you are living. You plant much but harvest little; you eat and drink but are never satisfied; you dress but are never warm; and your wages vanish as if into a bag with holes.
items.core_idea: Look at your ways: much effort, little satisfaction

items.plain: Our high priest understands our weaknesses, because he was tempted in every way as we are, yet did not sin. So let us come boldly to God's throne of grace to receive mercy and help when we need it.
items.core_idea: Jesus understands our weakness; approach God boldly

items.plain: So do not throw away your confidence; it will be richly rewarded. You need endurance, so that after doing God's will you receive what he promised.
items.core_idea: Keep your confidence; endurance brings the promise

items.plain: Faith is being sure of what we hope for and convinced of what we cannot see.
items.core_idea: Faith is confidence in the hoped-for and unseen

items.plain: By faith Abraham obeyed when God called him to go to the land he would inherit; he set out without knowing where he was going.
items.core_idea: Faith sets out without knowing where

items.plain: Since so many faithful witnesses surround us, let us drop every burden and the sin that trips us, and run our race with endurance, eyes on Jesus, who endured the cross for the joy ahead.
items.core_idea: Drop every weight and run with endurance

items.plain: Discipline feels painful, not pleasant, at the time, but later it brings the peace of right living to those trained by it. So strengthen your tired hands and weak knees, and walk straight paths so injuries can heal.
items.core_idea: Painful discipline later yields peace

items.plain: Keep loving each other as family. Welcome strangers, because some have hosted angels without knowing it. Remember prisoners as if you were in prison with them, and those who are mistreated, since you have a body too.
items.core_idea: Love, welcome strangers, remember those who suffer

items.plain: Do not love money; be content with what you have, because God has promised never to leave or abandon you. So we can say boldly that the Lord helps us and we will not fear what anyone can do.
items.core_idea: Be content; God will never leave you

items.plain: Let us return to God. He has torn and wounded us, but he will heal us and soon raise us to live before him. Let us strive to know him; he will come as surely as sunrise, like spring rain.
items.core_idea: Return to God; he will heal what he wounded

items.plain: God wants mercy, not sacrifice; he wants people to know him more than he wants burnt offerings.
items.core_idea: God wants mercy more than ritual

items.plain: Sow what is right and you will reap kindness. Break up your hard, unplowed ground, because it is time to seek God until he comes and showers righteousness on you.
items.core_idea: Break up hard ground and seek God

items.plain: Wash yourselves clean and put your evil deeds out of God's sight. Stop doing wrong and learn to do right: seek justice, help the oppressed, defend orphans and stand up for widows.
items.core_idea: Stop doing wrong; learn to do right

items.plain: God invites the people to talk things through: even if their sins are bright red like scarlet, they will become white as snow and wool.
items.core_idea: Though sins are scarlet, they can be white as snow

fix.display_text: “Come now, and let us reason together,” says Yahweh: “Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow. Though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

items.plain: Nations will no longer raise swords against one another, and they will not train for war any more.
items.core_idea: Nations will stop learning war

items.plain: Stop putting your trust in human beings; their life is only a breath, so what are they really worth?
items.core_idea: Do not rely on mere mortals

items.plain: Shame on those who keep buying up house after house and field after field until there is no room left for anyone, and they end up living alone in the land.
items.core_idea: Endless acquiring leaves you alone

items.plain: Shame on those who call evil good and good evil, who swap darkness for light and bitter for sweet. Shame on those who think themselves wise and clever.
items.core_idea: Woe to those who call evil good

items.plain: The prophet cried out that he was ruined, a man with unclean lips living among people with unclean lips, because he had seen God, the King.
items.core_idea: Seeing God, I see my own unworthiness

items.plain: I heard the Lord ask whom he should send and who would go. I answered: here I am, send me.
items.core_idea: Here I am; send me

items.plain: People who walked in darkness have seen a great light; light has shone on those living in the shadow of death.
items.core_idea: Light has dawned on those in darkness

items.plain: The people boasted: the brick buildings have fallen, but we will rebuild in cut stone; the fig trees are cut down, but we will plant cedars instead.
items.core_idea: Proud boast: we will rebuild bigger

items.plain: Can an axe boast against the one who swings it, or a saw against the one who uses it? That would be like a stick trying to lift the person holding it.
items.core_idea: A tool cannot boast against its user

items.plain: The wolf will live with the lamb and the leopard lie down with the young goat; calf and lion will be together, and a little child will lead them.
items.core_idea: Enemies at peace, led by a child

items.plain: God is my salvation; I will trust him and not be afraid, because the Lord is my strength and my song and has saved me.
items.core_idea: I trust God and will not be afraid

items.plain: The proud one who planned to climb above the stars and make himself like the Most High has fallen from heaven like the morning star, and will be brought down to the depths of the grave.
items.core_idea: Pride that reaches for heaven falls to the pit

items.plain: Give advice and do justice. Shelter the outcasts like shade at midday; hide them, and do not betray those who are fleeing.
items.core_idea: Shelter outcasts; do not betray the fugitive

items.plain: My heart is racing and horror has seized me; the evening I longed for has turned to trembling.
items.core_idea: The evening I longed for became dread

items.plain: Someone calls to the watchman asking how much of the night is left. The watchman answers that morning is coming, but night too; ask again if you wish, and come back.
items.core_idea: Morning comes, and night too

items.plain: God will swallow up death for ever and wipe the tears from every face, and remove his people's disgrace from the whole earth, because God has said so.
items.core_idea: God will end death and wipe away all tears

items.plain: God keeps in perfect peace those whose minds stay fixed on him because they trust him. So trust God for ever; he is a rock that lasts for ever.
items.core_idea: Trust in God keeps the mind in perfect peace

items.plain: I long for you, God, through the night, and seek you with all my spirit, because when your judgements are seen on earth, people learn what is right.
items.core_idea: I long for God in the night

items.plain: Like a woman in labour crying out in pain, we have suffered before you, God, but have given birth only to wind; we have achieved no rescue on the earth.
items.core_idea: We laboured in pain and produced only wind

items.plain: Go into your rooms, my people, and shut the doors. Hide for a little while until the anger has passed.
items.core_idea: Shelter a little while until it passes

items.plain: God says you will be saved by turning back and resting; your strength will come from quietness and trust.
items.core_idea: Strength lies in quietness and trust

items.plain: Even if God gives you hardship and suffering to live on, your teachers will no longer be hidden; whichever way you turn, you will hear a voice behind you saying, this is the way, walk in it.
items.core_idea: Even in hardship you will hear: this is the way

items.plain: Each person will be like a shelter from the wind and storm, like streams in a dry land, like the shade of a great rock in a weary country.
items.core_idea: A person can be shelter for others

items.plain: Doing right will bring peace, and its result will be quiet and confidence for ever. God's people will live in peaceful homes, safe and quietly at rest.
items.core_idea: Righteousness brings peace, quiet and safety

items.plain: Lord, be kind to us; we have waited for you. Be our strength every morning and our rescue in times of trouble.
items.core_idea: God, be our strength every morning

items.plain: The wilderness and dry land will be glad; the desert will rejoice and bloom like a rose.
items.core_idea: The desert will bloom

items.plain: Strengthen tired hands and weak knees. Tell the frightened to be strong and not afraid, because their God is coming to set things right and save them.
items.core_idea: Be strong, do not fear; God will save you

items.plain: Gravely ill, King Hezekiah said he was going to the grave in mid-life, robbed of his remaining years, never again to see God or people among the living; his life was being cut off like cloth from a loom.
items.core_idea: Lament at life cut off in its middle

items.plain: I suffered bitterly instead of having peace, but in your love you saved my life from the pit and threw all my sins behind your back.
items.core_idea: God in love saved me and cast my sins away

items.plain: God tells his messengers to comfort his people. Speak tenderly to Jerusalem: her hard service is over, her guilt is forgiven, and she has paid twice over for her sins.
items.core_idea: Comfort my people: their hardship is over

items.plain: A voice is told to cry out a message: all people are like grass, and their glory like wild flowers. The grass withers and the flower fades when God's breath blows, but God's word lasts for ever.
items.core_idea: People fade like grass; God's word endures

items.plain: God will come in power and rule. Yet he will care for his flock like a shepherd: he gathers the lambs in his arms, carries them close, and gently leads the mothers with young.
items.core_idea: God carries his lambs like a gentle shepherd

items.plain: The eternal God, creator of the earth, never tires, and his understanding has no limit. He strengthens the weak. Even the young grow tired and fall, but those who wait for God will renew their strength and soar like eagles.
items.core_idea: Those who wait for God renew their strength

items.plain: Do not be afraid, because I am with you; do not lose heart, because I am your God. I will strengthen you, help you, and hold you up with my righteous right hand.
items.core_idea: Do not fear; God is with you and upholds you

items.plain: God presents his chosen servant, filled with his Spirit, who will bring justice to the nations. He will not shout or make a show; he will not break a bruised reed or snuff out a faint flame.
items.core_idea: God's servant is gentle with the bruised and faint

items.plain: God says he will lead the blind along roads and paths they do not know, turn their darkness into light and their crooked places straight, and never abandon them.
items.core_idea: God leads the blind on unknown paths

items.plain: God, who created and formed his people, says: do not be afraid, because I have rescued you. I have called you by name; you are mine.
items.core_idea: Do not fear; God called you by name

items.plain: When you go through deep waters, I will be with you, and the rivers will not sweep you away. When you walk through fire, you will not be burned, and the flames will not hurt you.
items.core_idea: Through water and fire, God is with you

items.plain: Do not dwell on the past or what happened long ago. God is doing something new; it is springing up now. He will make a road through the wilderness and rivers in the desert.
items.core_idea: Forget the past; God is doing a new thing

items.plain: God says he has wiped away your wrongdoings and sins like a thick cloud; come back to him, because he has rescued you.
items.core_idea: Your sins are wiped away; return to God

items.plain: God tells his people that he has carried them since birth, and he will go on carrying them into old age and grey hair. He made them, and he will bear them, carry them and rescue them.
items.core_idea: God carries you from birth to old age

items.plain: God says he has refined his people, though not the way silver is refined; he chose them in the furnace of suffering.
items.core_idea: Chosen in the furnace of suffering

items.plain: If only you had listened to my commands! Then your peace would have flowed like a river, and your goodness would have rolled on like the waves of the sea.
items.core_idea: Heeding God brings peace like a river

items.plain: I thought my work had been useless and my strength spent for nothing; yet what is due to me rests with God, and my reward is with him.
items.core_idea: Though effort seems wasted, God holds my reward

items.plain: Zion said God had abandoned and forgotten her. God answers: could a mother forget her nursing baby? Even if she could, I will not forget you. I have written you on the palms of my hands.
items.core_idea: God will never forget you

items.plain: God has taught me how to speak so that my words can hold up someone who is weary. Every morning he wakes me to listen like a student.
items.core_idea: God teaches words that sustain the weary

items.plain: Because God helps me, I have not been put to shame. So I have set my face like stone, knowing I will not be let down.
items.core_idea: With God's help, I set my face like flint

items.plain: Whoever honours God but walks in darkness with no light should trust in God's name and lean on their God.
items.core_idea: In darkness without light, trust God

items.plain: Look at the sky and the earth: the heavens will vanish like smoke and the earth wear out like clothing, and its people will die too. But God's salvation lasts for ever, and his justice will never end.
items.core_idea: All things pass; God's salvation lasts for ever

items.plain: God tells those who hold his law in their hearts: do not fear people's scorn or be shaken by their insults. They will be eaten away like moth-eaten cloth, but God's justice and salvation last for ever.
items.core_idea: Do not fear people's insults; they will pass

items.plain: God says: I am the one who comforts you. Why fear mortals who wither like grass, and forget God your Maker who spread out the heavens? Why live in constant fear of the oppressor's fury? Where is that fury now?
items.core_idea: Why fear mortals when God comforts you?

items.plain: How beautiful is the arrival of the messenger crossing the mountains with good news of peace and salvation, telling Zion that its God reigns.
items.core_idea: Beautiful are those who bring good news

items.plain: God says he abandoned his people for a brief moment, but will gather them back with great mercy; in a flash of anger he hid his face, but his everlasting love will have mercy on them.
items.core_idea: Brief abandonment, everlasting mercy

items.plain: Even if the mountains are moved and the hills shaken, God's steadfast love will not leave you, and his promise of peace will not be taken away.
items.core_idea: God's love outlasts the mountains

items.plain: Come, all who are thirsty, come to the water; even with no money, come and eat for free. Why spend money on what is not food, and work for what never satisfies? Listen to God and feed your soul.
items.core_idea: Why spend yourself on what does not satisfy?

items.plain: God says his thoughts and ways are not like ours: as the heavens are higher than the earth, so his ways and thoughts are higher than ours.
items.core_idea: God's ways are higher than our ways

fix.display_text: “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not my ways,” says Yahweh. “For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.

items.plain: You will go out with joy and be led in peace. The mountains and hills will burst into song before you, and all the trees will clap their hands.
items.core_idea: You will go out in joy and peace

items.plain: Good people die and no one takes it to heart; the kind are taken away and no one realises they are spared from coming evil. They enter peace and rest, those who lived upright lives.
items.core_idea: The righteous who die enter peace

items.plain: The high and holy God, who lives for ever, says he lives in the high and holy place, and also with those who are crushed and humble in spirit, to revive them.
items.core_idea: God dwells with the humble and crushed in spirit

items.plain: The fast God wants is this: break the chains of injustice and free the oppressed; feed the hungry, shelter the homeless poor, clothe the naked, and do not turn from your own. Then your light will break out like dawn.
items.core_idea: True devotion is freeing the oppressed and feeding the hungry

items.plain: We hope for light but find darkness, for brightness but walk in gloom. We feel along the wall like the blind and stumble at noon as if it were dusk; among the strong we are like the dead.
items.core_idea: We look for light but walk in darkness

items.plain: Get up and shine, because your light has come and God's glory has risen on you. Darkness will cover the earth and its peoples, but God will rise on you and his glory will be seen on you.
items.core_idea: Arise, shine: your light has come

items.plain: You will no longer need the sun or moon for light, because God will be your everlasting light and your glory. Your sun will never set again, and your days of mourning will be over.
items.core_idea: God will be your light; mourning will end

items.plain: The speaker says God's Spirit has anointed him to bring good news to the humble, heal the broken-hearted, free captives, and comfort all who mourn, giving them beauty for ashes, joy for mourning and praise for despair.
items.core_idea: Sent to heal the broken-hearted and comfort mourners

items.plain: I will rejoice greatly in God, and my soul will be glad, because he has dressed me in salvation and righteousness, like a groom in his garland or a bride in her jewels.
items.core_idea: I rejoice: God has clothed me in salvation

items.plain: You will no longer be called Forsaken, nor your land Desolate. You will be called My Delight, and your land Married, because God delights in you.
items.core_idea: No longer forsaken: God delights in you

items.plain: In all their suffering God suffered too, and his presence saved them. In love and pity he rescued them, and lifted and carried them through all the years of old.
items.core_idea: God suffers with his people and carries them

items.plain: We have all become unclean, and even our good deeds are like filthy rags. We all wither like leaves, and our sins sweep us away like the wind.
items.core_idea: Our sins sweep us away like leaves

items.plain: Yet, God, you are our Father. We are the clay and you are the potter; we are all the work of your hands.
items.core_idea: We are clay; God is the potter

items.plain: God says he is creating new heavens and a new earth, and the past will be forgotten. Rejoice for ever in what he creates. He will delight in his people, and weeping will never be heard in Jerusalem again.
items.core_idea: God makes all things new; weeping will end

items.plain: God says that before people call he will answer, and while they are still speaking he will hear.
items.core_idea: God answers before we call

items.plain: God says he will comfort you as a mother comforts her child.
items.core_idea: God comforts like a mother

items.plain: When you face all kinds of trials, consider it pure joy, because testing your faith builds endurance. Let endurance finish its work, so that you become mature and complete, lacking nothing.
items.core_idea: Trials build endurance; welcome them with joy

items.plain: If you lack wisdom, ask God, who gives generously to all without scolding, and you will receive it. But ask in faith without doubting; a doubter is like a wind-tossed wave, unstable, and should expect nothing from the Lord.
items.core_idea: Ask God for wisdom, in faith without doubting

items.plain: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to get angry, because human anger does not produce the goodness God wants.
items.core_idea: Quick to listen, slow to speak and anger

items.plain: Do what God's word says; just listening fools you. A mere listener is like someone who sees their face in a mirror and forgets it at once. Whoever keeps to the law of freedom and acts will be blessed.
items.core_idea: Do what you hear, not only listen

items.plain: Pure religion in God's eyes is this: caring for orphans and widows in their distress, and keeping yourself from being corrupted by the world.
items.core_idea: True religion: care for the vulnerable, stay unstained

items.plain: What use is saying you have faith if you do nothing? If someone lacks clothes and food and you just wish them well without giving what they need, what good is that? Faith without action is dead.
items.core_idea: Faith without action is dead

items.plain: A small bit steers a horse, and a small rudder steers a huge ship through strong winds. The tongue is small too, yet it boasts of great things. Think how a tiny spark sets a whole forest on fire.
items.core_idea: The small tongue has huge power

items.plain: If you are wise, show it by good deeds done gently. Bitter jealousy and selfish ambition are not wisdom from above; they bring disorder and evil. Wisdom from above is pure, peaceful, gentle, merciful and sincere, and peacemakers reap righteousness.
items.core_idea: True wisdom is gentle and peaceful, not envious

items.plain: Fights come from the desires warring inside you. You want what you cannot have, so you fight. You do not have because you do not ask God, and when you ask, you ask only for your own pleasures.
items.core_idea: Conflict comes from selfish desires
